title: Kazia Therapeutics Announces Two Abstracts on Paxalisib Tumor and Immune Reprogramming Research Accepted for Poster Presentation at 2026 San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium

*Presentations to Explore Paxalisib's Differentiated Tumor and Immune Reprogramming Activity*


SYDNEY


, Nov. 2, 2026


/PRNewswire/ --[Kazia Therapeutics Limited](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4811635-1&h=2007642925&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.kaziatx.com%2F&a=Kazia+Therapeutics+Limited) (NASDAQ: KZIA) ("Kazia" or the "Company"), an oncology-focused biotechnology company developing therapies that selectively reprogram cancer biology, restore anti-tumor immunity and overcome treatment resistance, today announced that two abstracts highlighting new preclinical and translational research on paxalisib's differentiated biological activity and potential application across breast cancer settings have been accepted for poster presentation at this year's[San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4811635-1&h=3400036333&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsabcs.org%2F&a=San+Antonio+Breast+Cancer+Symposium) ("SABCS"), taking place on Dec. 8 through 11, 2026, in San Antonio, Texas.


The presentations will explore two complementary areas of research: the distinct tumor and immune reprogramming effects of paxalisib compared with other dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitors in preclinical models, and its potential to suppress local recurrence and metastatic progression when administered following standard neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in a preclinical model of stage III triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC):


- **Poster 1 (P4-9-18)** : "Paxalisib uniquely induces durable tumour and immune reprogramming across breast cancer subtypes, challenging the paradigm that dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitors are biologically equivalent"
- **Poster 2 (P4-10-26):** "Suppression of Local and Metastatic Recurrence by Adjuvant PI3K/mTOR Inhibition Through Durable Immune Epigenetic Rewiring Following Neoadjuvant Chemo-Immunotherapy in Stage III Triple-Negative Breast Cancer"


The research further explores paxalisib's differentiated ability to reprogram tumor and immune biology in preclinical models, suggesting that these effects are not necessarily shared by other dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitors. Kazia believes this emerging evidence supports a mechanism of action that extends beyond conventional kinase inhibition.


**About Kazia Therapeutics Limited**


Kazia Therapeutics Limited (NASDAQ: KZIA) is an oncology-focused biotechnology company developing therapies that selectively reprogram cancer biology, restore anti-tumor immunity and overcome treatment resistance. Kazia's lead asset, paxalisib, is an investigational oral, brain-penetrant dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor being developed across multiple forms of cancer, including cancers of the central nervous system, advanced breast cancer and colorectal cancer. Paxalisib has received U.S. FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations for glioblastoma, Fast Track designation for PI3K-altered brain metastases with radiation and Rare Pediatric Disease and Orphan Drug designations for select pediatric brain tumors, including diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma and atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor.


Kazia is also advancing two potentially first-in-class preclinical programs: NDL2, a nuclear PD-L1 protein degrader targeting a newly identified mechanism of immunotherapy resistance and metastatic progression, and MSETC, a SETDB1 inhibitor intended to restore immune signaling in tumors that have become resistant to immunotherapy, including checkpoint inhibitors. Additionally, Kazia's portfolio includes EVT801, a small molecule VEGFR-3 inhibitor that the Company is exploring for potential partnering opportunities.
